certificate.detail: a nonconstant map of degree 3 from y^2 = g to the genus-1 curve v^2 = (-24*w)u^3 + (1/2*(27*w - 117))u^2 + (27*w + 9)u + (9) over X^2 + 3, (x,y) -> (p/q, y*hh/q^2) with p = x^2 + x, q = x^3 + (-w + 1)*x^2 + 1/6*(-5*w - 3)*x + 1/3*(w - 1), hh = x^3 + 1/2*(-w + 3)*x^2 - 2/3*w*x + 1/3*(-w - 1); degree-3 map, defined over Q(sqrt(-3)), from y^2 = g to a genus-1 curve; found by code/gsplit_cover3.m (torsion_jac, 2026-10-16)

reference: LMFDB extended genus 2 database (Booker–Sutherland), curve 6804.a.1 (table g2c_curves_new, label 6804.a1 on devmirror.lmfdb.xyz, read 2026-10-16); it is the curve C_3 of F. Leprévost, Jacobiennes de certaines courbes de genre 2: torsion et simplicité, J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 7 (1995), 283–306, p. 303 (the member t = 3 of the [3,9] family C_t), reprinted in Platonov–Zhgun–Petrunin 2013, p. 321 (credit corrected 2026-10-20)
notes: First Q-simple, geometrically split example of [3,9] for the census (the gsplit cell is empty). Found by querying the LMFDB genus 2 data (devmirror.lmfdb.xyz, g2c_curves_new: is_simple_base = true, is_simple_geom = false); smallest-conductor curve of this torsion group there (LMFDB conductor 6804). The automatic Richelot certificates do not apply (over Q(sqrt(-3)) the working model factors as two cubics and has no Richelot isogeny), so a splitness certificate is supplied: an explicit degree-3 map to a genus-1 curve over Q(sqrt(-3)) (the field over which J splits; the cubic factors of g are the fibre over the point at infinity and the three remaining Weierstrass points). Checked locally with the census's own pipeline/magma/verify_lib.m (Magma V2.30-1). Submitted by F. Najman; the curve is Leprévost's C_3 (1995, see Reference), found in the database cited there, and the cover was computed for this submission.
